reference_title: Eurocode 7: Geotechnical design - Part 2: Ground investigation and testing
chapter_title: Soil and rock sampling and groundwater measurements

sections.title: General
sections.summary: Sampling of soil and rock by drilling and excavation, and groundwater measurements, shall be comprehensive enough to obtain the geotechnical data needed for design.
sections.body: (1)P Sampling of soils and rocks by drilling and excavation, and groundwater measurements, shall be conducted comprehensively enough that the necessary geotechnical design data are obtained. (p. 33)
key_points: Sampling and groundwater measurements shall yield the design data needed (p. 33).
sections.applicability: General requirement framing the whole of Section 3.

sections.title: Sampling by drilling
sections.summary: Drilling equipment is chosen for the required sampling categories (3.4.1, 3.5.1), depth and sample diameter, and rig functions (recording of drilling parameters, automatic or manual adjustment), following EN ISO 22475-1.
sections.body: (1)P Drilling equipment shall be selected for the sampling categories required (3.4.1 and 3.5.1), the depth and sample diameter, and the rig functions needed (recording of drilling parameters, automatic or manual adjustment). (2)P EN ISO 22475-1 shall be followed. (p. 33)
key_points: Select drilling equipment by sampling category, depth and sample diameter (p. 33).
Follow EN ISO 22475-1 for sampling by drilling (p. 33).
sections.applicability: Equipment-selection rule for any drilling-based sampling programme.

sections.title: Sampling by excavation
sections.summary: Samples recovered from trial pits, headings or shafts shall follow the requirements of EN ISO 22475-1 for sampling by excavation.
sections.body: (1)P Samples recovered from trial pits, headings or shafts shall follow the requirements of EN ISO 22475-1. (p. 33)
key_points: Sampling by excavation follows EN ISO 22475-1 (p. 33).
sections.applicability: Equipment/procedure rule for excavation-based sampling (as opposed to drilling).

sections.title: Soil sampling
sections.summary: Heading for soil sampling: sampling categories and laboratory quality classes (3.4.1), identification (3.4.2), planning (3.4.3) and handling, transport and storage (3.4.4).
sections.body: Heading for 3.4.1 to 3.4.4; it has no text of its own. (p. 33)
sections.applicability: Governs the selection of soil sampling method and category to achieve the sample quality class needed for the intended laboratory tests.

sections.title: Categories of sampling methods and laboratory quality classes of samples
sections.summary: Samples must hold all the stratum's mineral constituents, uncontaminated. Three sampling categories (EN ISO 22475-1): A gives quality classes 1 to 5, B 3 to 5, C only 5. Classes 1 and 2 (structure, water content and void ratio as in situ) need category A; B keeps constituents and water content but disturbs structure; C changes structure and layering. Table 3.1 defines the five classes.
sections.body: (1)P Samples shall contain all mineral constituents of their strata, uncontaminated by other strata or sampling additives. (2)P Three sampling method categories (EN ISO 22475-1) apply by desired quality (Table 3.1): category A can give quality classes 1 to 5, B classes 3 to 5, C only class 5. (3) Classes 1 or 2 need category A: no or slight disturbance of structure, in-situ water content and void ratio, no change of constituents or chemistry; unforeseen conditions such as variable strata may lower the class. (4) Category B cannot give better than class 3: all constituents in original proportions and natural water content, layers identifiable, structure disturbed (p. 33). (5) Category C cannot give better than class 5: structure totally changed, layering modified so in-situ layers cannot be identified accurately, water content not necessarily natural. (6)P Laboratory soil samples fall in five quality classes by the properties assumed unchanged through sampling, handling, transport and storage, given in Table 3.1 with the sampling category to use (p. 34). (pp. 33 to 34)
key_points: Samples shall contain all mineral constituents and be uncontaminated (p. 33).
Category A gives classes 1 to 5, B classes 3 to 5, C only class 5 (p. 33).
Quality classes 1 or 2 can only be obtained by category A methods (p. 33).
Category C samples need not have the natural water content (p. 34).
tables: Table 3.1: Quality classes of soil samples for laboratory testing and sampling categories to be used - soil properties by quality class 1 to 5, as printed (classes marked). Unchanged soil properties: particle size 1, 2, 3, 4; water content 1, 2, 3; density, density index, permeability 1, 2; compressibility, shear strength 1. Properties that can be determined: sequence of layers 1, 2, 3, 4, 5; boundaries of strata - broad 1, 2, 3, 4; boundaries of strata - fine 1, 2; Atterberg limits, particle density, organic content 1, 2, 3, 4; water content 1, 2, 3; density, density index, porosity, permeability 1, 2; compressibility, shear strength 1. Sampling category according to EN ISO 22475-1: A spans classes 1 to 5, B classes 3 to 5, C class 5
sections.applicability: Governs the selection of soil sampling method and category to achieve the sample quality class needed for the intended laboratory tests.

sections.title: Soil identification
sections.summary: Soil identification, from examination of the recovered samples, shall conform to EN ISO 14688-1 (identification and description of soil).
sections.body: (1)P Soil identification, based on examination of the recovered samples, shall conform to EN ISO 14688-1. (p. 34)
key_points: Soil identification conforms to EN ISO 14688-1 (p. 34).
sections.applicability: Governs the selection of soil sampling method and category to achieve the sample quality class needed for the intended laboratory tests.

sections.title: Planning of soil sampling
sections.summary: Quality class and number of samples follow the investigation aims, geology and complexity. Drilling may recover the whole soil column or samples only at set levels; categories are chosen from Table 3.1, soil types and groundwater, equipment per EN ISO 22475-1. Sample size suits the tests; sample at each stratum change and usually at spacings of not more than 3 m.
sections.body: (1)P The quality class and number of samples shall be based on the aims of the investigation, the site geology and the complexity of the geotechnical structure and construction. (2) Sampling by drilling may follow two strategies: drilling that recovers the complete soil column, with samples from the drilling tools and from special samplers at chosen depths at the borehole bottom (p. 34); or drilling that recovers samples only at predetermined levels, e.g. set by separately conducted penetration tests. (3)P Sampling categories shall be selected for the laboratory quality classes wanted (Table 3.1), the expected soil types and the groundwater conditions. (4)P EN ISO 22475-1 governs the choice of drilling or excavation methods and sampling equipment for the prescribed category. NOTE: fully undisturbed samples are practically impossible (mechanical disturbance and stress release); disturbance depends on the category and especially the soil type, very sensitive soils being prone to it while most stiff clays allow less restrictive methods; each problem needs its own accuracy, so the sampling programme should decide the acceptable disturbance and hence the methods. (5) Specific equipment and methods within the 3.4.1 categories may be needed, e.g. to determine small-strain deformation moduli (stiffness) on undisturbed samples. (6)P Sample dimensions shall suit the soil type and the type and number of tests (NOTE: see Section 5 and Annexes L, M, N, P, Q, R and S). (7) Samples should be taken at every change of stratum and at a specified spacing, usually not more than 3 m; in inhomogeneous soil, or where a detailed ground definition is needed, continuous sampling by drilling or samples at very short intervals should be used (p. 35). (pp. 34 to 35)
key_points: Quality class and number of samples follow aims, geology and structure complexity (p. 34).
Choose sampling categories from Table 3.1, soil types and groundwater (p. 35).
Completely undisturbed samples are practically impossible; sensitive soils disturb most (p. 35).
Sample at each change of stratum, usually at spacings of not more than 3 m (p. 35).
Continuous sampling in inhomogeneous soil or where detailed definition is needed (p. 35).
sections.applicability: Governs the selection of soil sampling method and category to achieve the sample quality class needed for the intended laboratory tests.

sections.title: Handling, transport and storing of samples
sections.summary: Handling, transport and storage of soil samples follow EN ISO 22475-1; Section 5 covers handling and storing in the laboratory.
sections.body: (1)P Handling, transport and storing of samples shall follow EN ISO 22475-1. NOTE: for handling and storing in the laboratory see Section 5. (p. 35)
key_points: Handling, transport and storage of samples per EN ISO 22475-1 (p. 35).
sections.applicability: Governs the selection of soil sampling method and category to achieve the sample quality class needed for the intended laboratory tests.

sections.title: Rock sampling
sections.summary: Heading for rock sampling: categories of sampling methods (3.5.1), rock identification (3.5.2), planning (3.5.3) and handling, transport and storing of samples (3.5.4).
sections.body: Heading for 3.5.1 to 3.5.4; it has no text of its own. (p. 35)
sections.applicability: Governs the selection of rock sampling method/category and the required rock-mass quality descriptors (RQD/TCR/SCR).

sections.title: Categories of sampling methods
sections.summary: Rock samples must hold all mineral constituents, uncontaminated, and discontinuities with their infill should be defined closely as they often control mass strength and deformation. Category A keeps rock structure and in-situ strength, deformation, water content, density, porosity and permeability; B keeps the pieces' properties and shows the discontinuity pattern; C totally changes structure.
sections.body: (1)P Samples shall contain all mineral constituents of the strata sampled, uncontaminated by other strata or additives. (2)P Discontinuities and their infilling often control the strength and deformation of the rock mass as a whole, so they shall be defined as closely as possible during sampling where those properties are needed (p. 35). (3)P Three sampling method categories shall be considered (EN ISO 22475-1) by sample quality: A, B and C. (4) Category A aims at samples with no or slight disturbance of the rock structure in sampling or handling; strength and deformation properties, water content, density, porosity and permeability correspond to in-situ values, with no change of constituents or chemistry; unforeseen conditions such as variable strata may lower the quality. (5) Category B aims at samples holding all constituents in their original proportions, the rock pieces keeping their strength and deformation properties, water content, density and porosity, and the general discontinuity arrangement identifiable; the mass structure is disturbed, and with it the strength, deformation, water content, density, porosity and permeability of the rock mass itself. (6) Category C totally changes the structure of the rock mass and its discontinuities; the rock may be crushed and some constituents or chemistry may change; rock type, matrix, texture and fabric can still be identified (p. 36). (pp. 35 to 36)
key_points: Discontinuities and infill often control rock mass strength and deformation (p. 35).
Category A: in-situ strength, deformation, water content, density, porosity and permeability (p. 36).
Category B: pieces keep properties; discontinuity arrangement identifiable (p. 36).
Category C: structure totally changed; rock type, matrix, texture and fabric identifiable (p. 36).
sections.applicability: Governs the selection of rock sampling method/category and the required rock-mass quality descriptors (RQD/TCR/SCR).

sections.title: Rock identification
sections.summary: Visual rock identification from rock masses and samples conforms to EN ISO 14689-1; weathering grades from fresh to decomposed follow its 4.2.4 and 4.3.4, discontinuity pattern, spacing and inclination its 4.3.3; RQD, TCR and SCR (EN ISO 22475-1) shall be determined.
sections.body: (1)P Visual rock identification shall rest on examination of the rock masses and samples, including all observations of decomposition and discontinuities, and conform to EN ISO 14689-1. (2)P Weathering classification shall relate to the geological processes and cover the grades from fresh rock to rock decomposed into soil, conforming to 4.2.4 and 4.3.4 of EN ISO 14689-1:2003. (3)P Discontinuities (bedding planes, joints, fissures, cleavages, faults) shall be quantified for pattern, spacing and inclination in unambiguous terms, conforming to 4.3.3 of EN ISO 14689-1:2003. (4)P Rock quality designation (RQD), total core recovery (TCR) and solid core recovery (SCR), as defined in EN ISO 22475-1, shall be determined. (p. 36)
key_points: Rock identification conforms to EN ISO 14689-1 (p. 36).
Weathering grades per 4.2.4 and 4.3.4 of EN ISO 14689-1:2003 (p. 36).
Discontinuity pattern, spacing and inclination per 4.3.3 of EN ISO 14689-1:2003 (p. 36).
Determine RQD, TCR and SCR as defined in EN ISO 22475-1 (p. 36).
sections.applicability: Governs the selection of rock sampling method/category and the required rock-mass quality descriptors (RQD/TCR/SCR).

sections.title: Planning of rock sampling
sections.summary: Characteristics and number of rock samples follow the investigation aim, geology and complexity; the sampling category follows the rock characteristics to preserve (3.5.1) and the rock and groundwater conditions; drilling, excavation and equipment per EN ISO 22475-1.
sections.body: (1)P The characteristics and number of samples shall be based on the aim of the investigations, the geology of the area and the complexity of the geotechnical structure and construction (p. 36). (2)P The sampling category shall be selected for the rock characteristics to be preserved (3.5.1) and the expected rock and groundwater conditions. (3)P EN ISO 22475-1 governs the selection of drilling or excavation methods and sampling equipment. (4) Specific equipment and methods within the 3.5.1 categories may be needed for a given project (p. 37). (pp. 36 to 37)
key_points: Number of rock samples follows aims, geology and complexity (p. 36).
Sampling category follows the rock characteristics to be preserved (p. 37).
sections.applicability: Governs the selection of rock sampling method/category and the required rock-mass quality descriptors (RQD/TCR/SCR).

sections.title: Handling, transport and storing of samples
sections.summary: After sampling and visual inspection, rock cores are preserved, handled and stored according to EN ISO 22475-1.
sections.body: (1)P After sampling and visual inspection, the cores shall be preserved, handled and stored according to EN ISO 22475-1. (p. 37)
key_points: Cores preserved, handled and stored per EN ISO 22475-1 (p. 37).
sections.applicability: Governs the selection of rock sampling method/category and the required rock-mass quality descriptors (RQD/TCR/SCR).

sections.title: Groundwater measurements in soils and rocks
sections.summary: Heading for groundwater measurements in soils and rocks: general (3.6.1), planning and execution (3.6.2) and evaluation of results (3.6.3).
sections.body: Heading for 3.6.1 to 3.6.3; it has no text of its own. (p. 37)
sections.applicability: Governs the design, execution, and evaluation of groundwater level and pore pressure monitoring for any geotechnical project.

sections.title: General
sections.summary: Groundwater measurements conform to 2.1.4 and use open or closed measuring systems installed in the ground; 3.6 covers positive pore pressures relative to atmospheric, not negative ones.
sections.body: (1)P Groundwater measurements shall conform to 2.1.4. (2)P The groundwater table or pore pressures in soil and rock shall be determined by installing open or closed groundwater measuring systems in the ground. NOTE: 3.6 applies to positive pore water pressures relative to atmospheric pressure; negative pore pressures are not considered. (p. 37)
key_points: Measure with open or closed systems installed in the ground (p. 37).
Only positive pore pressures relative to atmospheric are covered (p. 37).
sections.applicability: Governs the design, execution, and evaluation of groundwater level and pore pressure monitoring for any geotechnical project.

sections.title: Planning and execution of the measurements
sections.summary: Equipment suits ground permeability, purpose, time, fluctuations and response. Open systems (observation wells) suit permeable ground and lag in low permeability; closed systems (transducers) suit all ground and should be used in very low permeability or high artesian pressure. Stations are sealed off; readings planned, adjusted, and spaced closer than the fluctuations measured.
sections.body: (1)P Groundwater measurement and sampling shall follow EN ISO 22475-1 when relevant. (2)P Equipment shall be selected for ground type and permeability, purpose, observation time, expected fluctuations and response time of equipment and ground. (3) Two main methods: open systems, where the piezometric head is measured in an observation well usually with an open pipe, and closed systems, where a pressure transducer measures the pressure at the chosen point directly. (4) Open systems suit relatively permeable soils and rock (aquifers and aquitards), e.g. sand, gravel or highly fissured rock; in low permeability they may mislead through the time lag of filling and emptying the pipe, which filter tips on a small-diameter hose reduce. (5) Closed systems can be used in all soils and rocks and should be used in very low permeability ground (aquicludes), e.g. clay or low fissured rock; they are also recommended for high artesian pressure (p. 37). (6)P Very short-term or fast pore pressure variations shall be monitored by continuous recording with transducers and data loggers. (7)P Open water within or near the area shall be considered in interpretation; well levels, springs and artesian water shall be noted. (8)P Number, location and depth of stations shall suit the purpose, topography, stratigraphy and soil conditions, especially permeability and aquifers. (9)P For monitoring projects (groundwater lowering, excavations, fills, tunnels) locations shall suit the changes expected. (10) Natural fluctuations should, if possible, be measured for reference outside the area the project affects. (11)P Measuring points shall be sealed off from other layers or aquifers according to EN ISO 22475-1. (12)P Number and frequency of readings and the measuring period shall be planned for the purpose and the stabilisation period. (13) The criteria should be adjusted after an initial period to the variations observed. (14)P To assess fluctuations, readings shall be at intervals smaller than the fluctuations and over a long period. (15) Water levels at the end of a drilling day and before drilling resumes the next day indicate groundwater conditions and should be recorded, as should sudden inflow or loss of water. (16) In early phases some boreholes may get filtered open perforated pipes; the following days' readings give a preliminary indication subject to the 3.6.2 (4) limits; the danger of connecting aquifers and environmental regulations should be considered (p. 38). (pp. 37 to 38)
key_points: Open systems suit permeable ground; time lag misleads in low permeability (p. 37).
Closed systems suit all ground; use them in aquicludes and for high artesian pressure (p. 37).
Fast pore pressure changes need continuous recording with transducers and loggers (p. 38).
Seal measuring points off from other layers or aquifers (p. 38).
Read at intervals smaller than the fluctuations, over a long period (p. 38).
Record water levels at end and start of drilling days and sudden inflow or loss (p. 38).
sections.applicability: Governs the design, execution, and evaluation of groundwater level and pore pressure monitoring for any geotechnical project.

sections.title: Evaluation of results of groundwater measurements
sections.summary: Evaluation accounts for geology, measurement accuracy, fluctuation with time, observation period, season and climate, reports observed maximum and minimum levels or pressures with the period, and where applicable derives cautious upper and lower bounds for extreme and normal circumstances. Annex C gives a statistical example using long-term regional reference records.
sections.body: (1)P Evaluation shall account for site geology and geotechnical conditions, accuracy of individual readings, pore pressure fluctuation with time, length of the observation period, season, and the climate during and before it (p. 38). (2)P Evaluated results shall give the observed maximum and minimum water table elevations or pore pressures and the measuring period. (3)P Where applicable, upper and lower bounds for extreme and normal circumstances shall be derived from the measurements by adding or subtracting the expected fluctuations, or a reduced part of them; frequent lack of long-term data makes the derived values a cautious estimate. (4) The need for further measurements or added stations should be assessed during the field investigations and in the ground investigation report. NOTE: Annex C gives an example of a statistical method for groundwater conditions where long-term readings in a regional reference pipe and a short measuring period on site exist (p. 39). (pp. 38 to 39)
key_points: Report observed maximum and minimum levels or pore pressures with the period (p. 39).
Derive cautious upper and lower bounds for extreme and normal circumstances (p. 39).
Annex C gives a statistical method using regional long-term records (p. 39).
sections.applicability: Governs the design, execution, and evaluation of groundwater level and pore pressure monitoring for any geotechnical project.
